title: Reliability and Effectiveness of Autonomous AI Agents in Supply Chain Management
abstract: arXiv:2605.17036v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: This paper studies the performance and reliability of autonomous generative AI agents in multi-echelon supply chains using the MIT Beer Game. We examine how model choice, operational guardrails, centralized data sharing, and prompt design affect system performance. In our best-performing configuration, GenAI agents reduce total supply-chain costs by up to 80% relative to human teams. Despite strong average performance, autonomous agents can exhibit substantial run-to-run instability, generating volatile procurement decisions and large tail costs. We characterize this phenomenon as agent bullwhip, the amplification of decision instability in autonomous multi-agent systems. We show that this instability can propagate across echelons and compound over time, even when the underlying demand path is held fixed. We then evaluate two approaches for improving reliability: reinforcement-learning post-training and operational guardrails.

translated_title: 自主AI智能体在供应链管理中的可靠性与有效性
translated_abstract: 本文利用MIT啤酒游戏研究了自主生成式AI智能体在多级供应链中的性能与可靠性。我们考察了模型选择、运营护栏、集中式数据共享以及提示词设计如何影响系统性能。在表现最佳的配置中，GenAI智能体相较于人类团队可将供应链总成本降低高达80%。尽管平均表现优异，自主智能体可能表现出显著的运行间不稳定性，产生波动的采购决策和巨大的尾部成本。我们将这一现象表征为“智能体牛鞭效应”，即自主多智能体系统中决策不稳定性的放大。我们表明，即使潜在需求路径保持不变，这种不稳定性也可能跨层级传播并随时间不断复合。随后，我们评估了两种提升可靠性的方法：强化学习后训练和运营护栏。
tldr: 该论文通过MIT啤酒游戏发现自主GenAI智能体可将供应链总成本降低高达80%，但会引发名为“智能体牛鞭效应”的决策不稳定性，并证明强化学习后训练与运营护栏可有效提升其可靠性。
en_tdlr: Using the MIT Beer Game, this paper shows that autonomous GenAI agents can cut total supply-chain costs by up to 80% versus human teams, but exhibit "agent bullwhip" decision instability, which can be mitigated through reinforcement-learning post-training and operational guardrails.
